subject: Life Skills
title: The Affect Labeling Trick
description: A fast breakdown of The Affect Labeling Trick for builders.

hook.text: UCLA researchers showed people photos of angry faces. Those who labeled the emotion felt less disturbed by it.

buildup.text: Affect labeling means putting a word to what you feel. It activates the prefrontal cortex, which calms the amygdala.

discovery.text: It works in real time. Silently saying 'I am feeling anxious' during a stressful moment measurably reduces your anxiety.

twist.text: It also works on other people. Saying 'You seem frustrated' to someone often de-escalates them faster than logic.

climax.text: Use it as a real-time tool. Tense meeting? Quietly label your emotion.

punchline.text: Name the feeling. The brain calms on command.

quiz.question: Why does labeling an emotion reduce its intensity?
options: It distracts you from the feeling
It activates the prefrontal cortex, which calms the amygdala
It forces you to smile, which changes your mood
